scope: Local zero-credential coordinator-owned trigger envelopes, durable waits, webhook ingress, callbacks and pull scheduler
implemented: Coordinator-owned generic trigger envelopes derive and enforce server scope
Event-routed trigger envelopes require complete trimmed missionId, eventType and eventKey identity before persistence
Trigger updates revalidate merged route identity and reject all persisted missionId changes, including explicit undefined clearing
Same-route trigger replays require the original causating trigger identity; distinct trigger IDs cannot be falsely applied
Business-event waits preserve expiry and restore through pause/resume with activeWait projection
SQL trigger persistence permits durable rejected claims while protecting immutable trigger identity and content on update
Trigger updates revalidate merged route identity and reject state-corrupting missionId changes
Trigger records persist durably before dispatch with immutable payload and complete routing identity
Identical trigger retries replay after application; RECEIVED/REJECTED records retry through the coordinator and conflicting reuse is rejected
Trigger lookups and updates are scope-qualified, allowing identical provider IDs in separate tenant scopes
Supplied Mission IDs are validated against the server-derived Mission ledger before acceptance
Project-bound webhook ingress routes through coordinator.trigger and returns a redacted durable acknowledgement
Governed trigger envelopes route mission/eventType/eventKey signals through the canonical business-event wait path
Unknown or non-Mission-specific trigger envelopes are durably accepted without mutating Mission state
Schedule trigger identities are deterministic from Mission ID and scheduled timestamp
Duplicate schedule triggers replay without creating duplicate waits or lifecycle events
Durable schedule and business-event waits persist in MissionStore and remain visible after coordinator restart
Pull scheduler ticks reconstruct due work from durable Mission and wait state rather than process-local timers
Due schedule waits activate WAITING_SCHEDULE to ACTIVE under the existing coordinator lock and Mission lease
Due deadline and non-schedule wait timeouts transition Missions to EXPIRED through the canonical lifecycle path
Public scheduleMission deadline creation is persisted and expires correctly after coordinator restart
Schedule environment is checked against the server-derived local environment before creation and activation
Terminal and cancelled Missions reject new schedules and scheduler callbacks
Matching business-event signals resolve active waits atomically; duplicate, unmatched and late signals fail closed
Provider callback identity, ordering, duplicate replay and conflicting identity are validated by the runtime
Terminal Mission delivery callbacks allow exact identity replay for completed and negative terminal outcomes; new or contradictory callbacks are fenced
Terminal direct delivery outcomes replay only when provider identity and outcome/code exactly match the durable outbox
Same-instance approval and callback replays retry persistence after an injected commit-write failure instead of reporting an undurable success
Trigger APPLIED/REJECTED status writes validate persistence results and preserve the original processing error when bookkeeping fails
Pause/resume restores deterministic schedule waits and active-wait projections
Concurrent scheduler tick and cancellation produce exactly one terminal lifecycle transition
Disposable worker SIGKILL tests cover receive, approval, delivery, pause, resume and cancel recovery
Existing inbound receive idempotency, approval ownership fencing and cancellation fencing remain coordinator-owned

coordinator, persistence reload and SQL parity tests reject tab, non-breaking-space and other ECMAScript-trim whitespace-only route identities
project webhook durable ingress and redacted response tests
business-event wait routing, duplicate registration and late signal tests
schedule duplicate, restart, pause/resume, environment and cancellation tests
public deadline creation and restart expiry tests
provider callback duplicate, ordering, identity, negative-terminal replay and completed-Mission fencing tests
direct permanent-delivery-rejection replay and delivered provider-identity collision tests
scheduler/cancellation race test with exactly one terminal transition
process-level SIGKILL recovery matrix and independent persisted-state verification
